channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Iran Boosts Air Defenses as It Braces For Fresh US Attacks
item.description: Iran said it’s strengthened its military defenses against a potential resumption of US strikes, the latest sign that the Islamic Republic is bracing for a return to all-out war as its tense standoff with Washington continues.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Sykes

item.title: Tourist Mecca Mauritius Extends Curfew After Riots, Looting
item.description: Mauritius, best known for its white-sand beach resorts, has extended a curfew for a further three nights, after the Indian Ocean island nation witnessed the worst unrest since 1999 earlier in the week.
item.dc:creator: Kamlesh Bhuckory and Antony Sguazzin

item.title: Ukraine Civilian Casualties Surge as Russia Intensifies Strikes
item.description: Civilian casualties in Ukraine jumped by 85% in September as Russia increased drone and missile attacks, according to the United Nations.
item.dc:creator: Daryna Krasnolutska

item.title: Poland Offers More NATO Troops If Allies Buy From Its Defense Industry
item.description: Poland is ready to send more troops to shore up NATO allies if those countries agree to sign contracts with its defense industry, Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Krasuski and Piotr Bujnicki

item.title: Investors Dial Back October Hike Bets After Warsh; Taiwan to Curb AI Chip Exports to China
item.description: US equity futures waver after rising on Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks at the IMF meetings. Taiwan is said to be preparing to tighten export controls on AI chips to further align with US restrictions, while the EU and China holds high-level trade talks. Russia is reportedly deploying an army of bots to push AI-fabricated videos and influence views on the US midterm elections. Arend Kapteyn of UBS speaks to Bloomberg's Lisa Abramowicz on "Bloomberg Brief" at the IIF annual meeting in Bangkok. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Midterm Mission: Turn Out Republicans
item.description: Democrats have the energy, but Republicans have the numbers — if they show up.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tamari

item.title: Prabowo Approval Sinks Below 50% as Economic Gloom Grows
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s approval rating has fallen to its lowest level since he took office, amid public concern about rising living costs and perceptions of worsening corruption in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Iron Ore Prices Should be Higher, Vale CEO Says
item.description: Vale CEO Gustavo Pimenta says iron ore prices should be “a little higher” as surging energy and freight costs make about 10% of global seaborne supply unprofitable. Iron ore futures in Singapore fell below $90 a ton this week for the first time in two years and are down about 15% in 2026. Speaking on "The Pulse With Francine Lacqua", Pimenta discussed Chinese demand, rising mining costs and what Brazil’s presidential election outcome could mean for the country’s mining sector. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Election Sees Lula, Bolsonaro Divide Over the Amazon Rainforest
item.description: Lula dramatically reduced deforestation that accelerated under Flávio Bolsonaro’s father while also supporting development.
item.dc:creator: Augusta Saraiva and Fabiano Maisonnave

item.title: Allianz CIO Sees up to 75 Bps of Fed Rate Hikes After Midterms
item.description: Ludovic Subran, chief investment officer and chief economist at Allianz, expects Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh to raise interest rates by as much as 75 basis points once the midterm elections are over. "The US is running hot, and I think he cannot ignore that," Subran tells Bloomberg Television. "I do expect the US will have to act decisively on inflation, both from energy, but also from AI," he adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Is Using an Army of Bots to Push Fake US Election Videos
item.description:
Fake videos of celebrities like Taylor Swift and Julia Roberts attacking Democratic candidates have started appearing on X.
Stephanie Baker explains how Russian disinformation operators are deploying an army of bots ahead of the US midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russian Bots Manipulate View Counts on Fake Videos Ahead of US Midterms
item.description: State-backed Matryoshka campaign targeting Democrats inflates view counts of fabricated stories, creating illusion of popularity.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Baker and Priyanjana Bengani

item.title: Albanian PM Blames Opposition for Stoking Angry Protests
item.description: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama accused the opposition and unnamed “foreign forces” of stoking violent protests, saying the demonstrations were an attempt to derail the country’s efforts to join the European Union.
item.dc:creator: Gresa Kraja

item.title: Romania Warns of Collateral Risk From Russian Black Sea Attacks
item.description: Russia is increasingly targeting Ukraine’s grain export corridors in the Black Sea and that increases security risks for the entire region, Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Andra Timu and Oliver Crook

item.title: The French Political Crisis Turning Into a Debt Crisis
item.description: Just about everyone is worried about what is going on in France right now: the country's public finances are in sorry shape and there are fears that the French bond selloff, and the country's growing debt crisis, might spillover into the rest of Europe. The 2027 elections have investors worried: Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon aren't seen to be up to the task of taming France's fiscal turmoil. Shahin Vallée was an advisor to Emmanuel Macron when he was an economic minister and during his first presidential election campaign. He is currently a senior fellow at the German Council of Foreign Relations and advises institutional investors — and he understands what went wrong during Macron's nine years in office. Today, he speaks to us about the origins of the current French debt crisis, how similar it is to the challenges Greece faced during the first euro crisis, and why the 2027 elections are making an unstable situation even worse. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Is Zelenskyy’s Only Ally Now: Latvia PM Kulbergs
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs says “Zelenskyy has only one ally now, it’s actually the Europeans,” as US-Ukraine tensions continue. He made the comments in an exclusive live interview with BTV’s Oliver Crook on the second day of the European leaders summit in Brussels on Friday (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Is Zelenskyy’s Only Ally Now, Latvian Leader Says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has only one ally now and that’s Europe, the Latvian prime minister said, referring to Kyiv’s spiraling tensions with the US.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis and Oliver Crook

item.title: Portugal Housing Protest Reflects Mounting Unease Across Europe
item.description: A housing protest in Portugal’s second-largest city, which was called off early Friday after clashes with the police, reflects growing unease across several other countries in Europe over the cost of living and housing affordability.
item.dc:creator: Henrique Almeida

item.title: Trump Seeks Culprits With Texas Senate Seat, Others in Peril
item.description: President Donald Trump railed at Senator John Cornyn of Texas and longtime GOP strategist Karl Rove, accusing them of undermining Ken Paxton’s Senate campaign in the state, a crucial contest for Republican hopes of retaining control of the chamber.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Bolsonaro, Lula in Tight Race Ahead of Runoff, Polls Show
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva are locked in a close race ahead of Brazil’s runoff election, according to two new polls.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati and Augusta Saraiva
